title: Redox-molecule monolayer turns each pillar into a pseudocapacitor
idea: Scale down to the molecule: graft a monolayer of fast one-electron redox molecules (ferrocene/viologen derivatives) onto the TiN pillar surface so each cell stores charge Faradaically in molecular orbitals, not only in the dielectric field. Electron transfer at a tethered monolayer is sub-ns and the molecules add ~10-30 uC/cm2 of switchable charge at <0.5 V swing.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 3-10x stored charge per pillar area lets AR drop from 60:1 toward 15-20:1, cutting etch steps and enabling lower VARY.

title: Ephemeral DRAM sized for millisecond data lifetimes
idea: Time-shift the retention spec from 64 ms to the real lifetime of AI activations and KV-cache tiles (often <2 ms between write and last read): build arrays with capacitors 4-5x smaller and short-pillar cells, tagged in the address map as 'ephemeral', and never refresh them; the runtime guarantees consume-before-expire.
why: Capacitor wall and refresh energy: ~4x smaller Cs, no refresh for that tier, roughly 30-40% lower cost per bit for activation memory.

title: CCD-style serial charge memory for streamed model weights
idea: Time-shift insight: inference reads weights in the same order every token, so random access is unnecessary. Store weights as charge packets clocked through buried-channel CCD shift registers (no per-bit access transistor, no bitline contact), tapped at the end by a single sense amp per 4k-bit chain.
why: Periphery and cell area: ~2-3F2 per bit and ~80% fewer sense amps; data movement drops because packets flow toward compute; targets 2-3x density for weight storage.

title: Relaxor polar-nanoregion dielectric for k near 70
idea: Scale down to 2-5 nm polar nanoregions: dope ZrO2/HfO2 laminates with La/Nb to make a relaxor-like dielectric whose nanoregions rotate freely under field (slim loop, no remanence), giving high effective permittivity without ferroelectric hysteresis loss.
why: Capacitor wall: Fact 1 says k~70 is the escape; relaxor behavior targets k 50-80 at 5 nm thickness, about 2x charge at today's AR.

title: 77 K immersion pods let storage capacitors shrink tenfold
idea: Jump from cell to datacenter scale: put memory sleds in liquid-nitrogen immersion pods where access-transistor leakage falls by ~6 orders, so retention goes from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor only needs to beat sense-amp offset, not leakage (~0.5 fF instead of 5 fF).
why: Capacitor wall and refresh: 10x smaller Cs, refresh eliminated, enabling short planar or 3D cells; cooling overhead amortized at rack scale.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium electrode inside every storage pillar
idea: Scale shift from battery-electrode science to the cell: deposit a Ru-Al alloy liner in the hole, selectively etch the Al to leave a 3-5 nm ligament nanosponge, then coat with ALD high-k and top electrode so one pillar has 3-5x internal surface area.
why: Capacitor wall: 3-5x Cs at the same footprint or same Cs at AR ~20:1, removing the hardest etch step.

title: Two-faced wafer: capacitors built on the thinned backside
idea: Borrow the wafer-scale backside-power trick: after front-side transistor and bitline processing, bond to a carrier, thin to 1 um and build the capacitor stack on the backside, connected by nano-vias through vertical access transistors, so capacitors no longer compete with bitlines and contacts.
why: Density and process: frees ~30-40% of front-side cell area and lets capacitors use full-cell footprint; enables 4F2 vertical-channel cells.

title: Transferred single-crystal SrTiO3 membrane as cell dielectric
idea: Scale shift across wafers: grow epitaxial SrTiO3 (k~300) on a sacrificial Sr3Al2O6 layer on a donor wafer at 800 C, release and transfer the membrane onto the low-temperature DRAM BEOL, then pattern stacked planar capacitors in it.
why: Capacitor wall: k~300 vs ~40 enables planar or low-AR (10:1) capacitors with 5 fF, removing high-AR etch and some EUV layers.

title: Time-domain sensing reads two bits per cell
idea: Time-shift the read: instead of a single voltage comparison, record how long the bitline takes to cross a threshold after charge sharing using a per-sense-amp time-to-digital counter; four charge levels map to four crossing times, storing 2 bits per capacitor.
why: Cost per bit: ~1.8x bits per cell area after margin; reuses existing capacitor process.

title: Ga2O3 ultra-wide-bandgap access transistor for hour retention
idea: Time-shift retention from 64 ms to ~1 hour by replacing the silicon access device with a 4.8 eV beta-Ga2O3 thin-film transistor, whose off-state leakage can be below 1e-21 A, while keeping a conventional stacked capacitor.
why: Refresh and leakage tail: refresh energy cut >1000x; Cs can shrink 3-5x because only sense margin matters.

title: Room-temperature single-electron box with electrometer readout
idea: Scale down to counting electrons: store tens of electrons on a sub-3 nm silicon or metal nanocluster whose charging energy exceeds kT at 300 K, read by an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current jumps with each electron.
why: Energy and density: write energy near aJ, cell footprint ~10 nm, attacking CV2 voltage floor.

title: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 phase switch pumps extra charge
idea: Scale down to the lattice: operate the capacitor dielectric as an antiferroelectric whose field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition releases a burst of polarization charge above a threshold voltage, then fully returns at zero field (no remanence, no wake-up fatigue).
why: Capacitor wall: 2-3x charge per pillar at the same AR; nonlinear charge also sharpens sense margin.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric layer amplifies cell capacitance
idea: Scale down to the domain level: insert a thin ferroelectric layer in series with the linear high-k so the ferroelectric operates in its negative-capacitance region, raising total stack capacitance above that of the high-k alone.
why: Capacitor wall: target 1.5-2x Cs without higher AR; hysteresis-free design keeps endurance unlimited.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterns capacitor holes without EUV
idea: Scale shift from polymer molecules to wafer patterns: use high-chi block copolymers that self-assemble into hexagonal cylinders at 16-20 nm pitch, guided by a coarse ArF template, to define the storage-node hole array.
why: Capital intensity: removes 1-2 EUV layers per cell array; molecules define the pitch for free.

title: Dual-mode cell parks its charge in a trap layer
idea: Jump timescales inside one cell: in active mode the bit lives on the capacitor (ns access); before idle or power-down, a high-voltage pulse pushes the state into an adjacent charge-trap nitride (years retention), and on wake it is restored to the capacitor.
why: Refresh power: idle refresh (16-33% of idle power) disappears; also gives instant-on persistence.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated nanolaminate capacitor at cell scale
idea: Scale down the multilayer ceramic capacitor from mm to nm: conformally deposit 4-6 alternating electrode/dielectric layers in each hole, with odd and even electrodes tied at opposite ends, so capacitance multiplies by layer count instead of by aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall: ~3x Cs at the same AR, or a 25:1 AR cell matching today's Cs.

title: Coaxial capacitor shell wraps the vertical access transistor
idea: Collapse two scales into one pillar: the vertical channel transistor sits in the core and the storage capacitor is a coaxial dielectric/electrode shell wrapped around its upper half, so a 4F2 footprint holds both.
why: Density: 6F2 to 4F2 (~33% area gain) without separate capacitor landing pads.

title: Microring resonance reads capacitor charge nondestructively
idea: Scale shift into photonics: the storage node is a pn junction embedded in a silicon microring; stored charge shifts the ring resonance by plasma dispersion, so a WDM probe beam reads hundreds of bits per waveguide without discharging them.
why: Destructive read and data movement: removes sense-amp restore and lets reads leave the die optically, ~1 pJ/bit target.

title: Significance-graded cell sizes for MSB and LSB bits
idea: Time-shift by bit importance: lay out arrays with large-capacitor cells for exponent and high bits and small, unrefreshed cells for low mantissa bits of AI weights and activations, which may decay gracefully between writes.
why: Cost per bit and refresh: ~25-35% area saving and half the refresh energy for FP16/BF16 tensors with negligible accuracy loss.

title: Deuterium isotope passivation trims the access-transistor leakage tail
idea: Scale down to the isotope: anneal in D2 instead of H2 so interface traps are capped with Si-D bonds, which resist desorption and trap-assisted tunneling more strongly over years of operation, shrinking the GIDL tail.
why: Leakage tail and refresh: if the worst tail drops 2-4x, refresh can be 2-4x rarer at 32-64 Gb; cheap drop-in.

title: Rack-scale erasure codes let cells skip most refreshes
idea: Jump from the cell to the rack: extend refresh to 1 s and accept that weak-tail cells flip, because data is striped with LDPC/erasure codes across 64 DRAM chips on several DIMMs; a rack scrubber repairs flips well before they accumulate.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth: ~15x fewer refreshes recovers 10-20% bandwidth and most idle refresh power.

title: Gen-10.5 display fabs print 1T1C memory panels
idea: Scale up from wafer to 3 m glass: every LCD pixel is already a TFT plus storage capacitor, so retool display fabs to print oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays at ~1 um rules across whole panels, diced into far-memory tiles.
why: Capital intensity and US manufacturability: panel cost ~$100-300/m2 makes a slower capacity tier at single-digit $/GB with no EUV and no Spruce Pine crucibles.

title: Weak-retention dies resold as short-refresh AI memory
idea: Time-shift the binning: rather than scrapping dies that fail 64 ms retention, bin them by tail and sell them qualified at 16-32 ms refresh for AI accelerators that refresh aggressively anyway.
why: Scarce supply: recovers a few percent of wafer output as sellable bits with zero new fab capacity.

title: Low-barrier magnetic tunnel junction refreshed like DRAM
idea: Time-shift the magnet's retention from 10 years to ~1 s by designing thermal stability near 25 kT; a small STT pulse writes it and a DRAM-like controller refreshes every few hundred ms, so the bit is held in spin, not charge.
why: Energy and endurance: write current ~5x lower than nonvolatile MRAM, essentially unlimited endurance, and a cell with no capacitor at ~20 F2.

title: Datacenter fiber loops store bits as light in flight
idea: Jump to datacenter scale and to time of flight: coil 10-50 km of fiber per rack and circulate WDM pulse trains with amplification; a 20 km loop at 64 channels x 100 Gb/s holds about 0.6 Gb in transit for streaming tensors.
why: Scarce resources: memory capacity from mature telecom fiber and lasers, with no DRAM wafers, for sequential-access buffers.

title: On-chip phononic delay line recirculates acoustic bit packets
idea: Shrink the 1940s mercury delay line to a chip: GHz bulk-acoustic pulses in AlScN/LiNbO3 waveguides travel 100,000x slower than light, so a 1 cm folded path holds micro-seconds of 10 Gb/s data, regenerated at each lap.
why: Capital and periphery: storage needs no cell array or access transistors, only transducers; serial buffer density per mm2 with a mature RF filter fab process.

title: Nanomechanical parametron stores bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale and GHz: a doubly clamped SiC beam pumped at twice its resonance oscillates in one of two phases (0 or pi), which is the bit; the pump sustains it every cycle and neighboring beams couple to shift data.
why: Endurance and leakage: no charge to leak and no wear-out; logic and memory share one element.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops hold persistent-current bits
idea: Pair cell scale with datacenter cryogenics: NbN nanowire loops 100-200 nm across store a fluxon as circulating supercurrent with indefinite retention at 4 K, read by a nanowire cryotron; deployed in cryo pods next to superconducting accelerators.
why: Energy: zJ-class writes and no refresh; kinetic inductance shrinks the loop well below magnetic-inductance limits.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayers switch by 1.4 angstrom registry shift
idea: Scale down to van der Waals stacking: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2 the bit is the AB versus BA stacking order, flipped by a sub-angstrom interlayer slide under field, with reported low fatigue because no ions move.
why: Endurance and voltage: sub-1 V switching, 1e10+ cycles target, wafer-scale 2D growth enables BEOL stacking.

title: 2D tunnel-diode bistable latch stacked in BEOL
idea: Shift the Goto-pair latch from III-V wafers to atomic layers: two WSe2/SnSe2 band-to-band tunnel diodes in series form a bistable node with negative differential resistance, plus one oxide access transistor, all in BEOL tiers.
why: 3D density: no capacitor, standby current in the pA range, stackable 10+ tiers over logic.

title: Power-grid thyristor shrunk to a 15 nm memory pillar
idea: Scale shift from grid-scale SCRs to a 15 nm vertical pnpn pillar: regenerative bipolar feedback latches the cell on or off, a gate pulse switches it, and a small holding bias keeps it, giving a 4F2 capacitor-free cell.
why: Density and process: 4F2 with no capacitor etch, fast read current 10x DRAM.

title: 3D NAND strings retuned for DRAM retention and endurance
idea: Time-shift flash from 10-year retention to ~1 s: thin the tunnel oxide to 1.5-2 nm direct tunneling so charge traps in a 200-tier vertical string write in ns with 1e15 cycles, refreshed like DRAM, using existing 3D NAND fabs.
why: Capital intensity and density: 200 stacked tiers built with mature NAND tools and no EUV, multi-x bits per mm2.

title: Thermostat-held VO2 phase bits in hysteresis window
idea: Couple chip and datacenter scales: hold the die by liquid cooling at the middle of a W-doped VO2 thermal hysteresis window, where both metal and insulator phases are stable; Joule pulses set metal and Peltier micro-coolers reset insulator.
why: Endurance and speed: ns electronic phase change without atomic migration; the facility cooling loop becomes part of the memory.

title: Contactless bistable buckled nanobeam snaps between two shapes
idea: Shrink the hair-clip snap-through to a 100 nm single-crystal SiC beam pre-buckled by film stress: the bit is up or down buckling, flipped electrostatically and read by piezoresistance, and it never touches a contact so it avoids stiction.
why: Endurance and leakage: nonvolatile, zero standby power, 1e12+ fatigue cycles in single-crystal SiC.

title: Skyrmion racetrack in synthetic antiferromagnet tubes
idea: Scale bits down to 10 nm topological spin whirls: compensated synthetic-antiferromagnet skyrmions have no Hall drift and move at km/s, so a vertical racetrack tube stores 64 bits per access device.
why: Density and periphery: one access device per 64 bits instead of per bit, 3D vertical tubes.

title: Magnetoelectric BiFeO3 flips nanomagnets with voltage alone
idea: Shift write energy to the atto-joule scale: a voltage across thin BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which exchange-couples to a CoFe free layer, writing a magnet with no current and reading it by TMR.
why: Voltage floor and energy: ~100 mV, aJ writes break the CV2 wall; no capacitor and no refresh.

title: Lithium niobate domain-wall conduction gives nondestructive reads
idea: Scale down to 1 nm domain walls: in wafer-bonded single-crystal LiNbO3 films a written ferroelectric domain creates a conducting wall between electrodes, so the bit is read by current without switching.
why: Destructive read and endurance: nondestructive read, 1e10+ cycles, single-crystal film from mature RF-filter wafers.

title: Altermagnet RuO2 or MnTe bits with picosecond dynamics
idea: Jump to the picosecond timescale: altermagnets have zero net moment like antiferromagnets yet spin-split bands, so the Neel-vector bit is written by spin-orbit torque in ps and read by tunneling magnetoresistance, with no stray-field crosstalk.
why: Density and energy: no stray fields allows tight pitch; ps switching at low current.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits held by bias light
idea: Shift storage into photon lifetime: an InP photonic-crystal nanocavity with carrier-plasma bistability sits on a shared continuous bias beam, and the bit is the high or low intracavity energy state; a pulse flips it.
why: Data movement: memory lives in the optical domain beside photonic interconnect, with ~fJ switching.

title: Spin-crossover molecules switch between high and low spin
idea: Scale down to one Fe(II) complex: spin-crossover molecules with wide room-temperature thermal hysteresis toggle high-spin and low-spin by field pulses, changing junction conductance by 10x.
why: Density: molecular-scale bits self-assembled in crossbars without lithography.

title: Molecular quantum-dot cellular automata loop memory
idea: Scale bits down to electron positions inside a 2 nm mixed-valence molecule: the bit is which diagonal pair of four redox sites holds two electrons, and a clocked ring of molecules circulates bits like a shift register.
why: Density and energy: THz switching with near kT energy, theoretical 1e14 bits/cm2.

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state in 1T-TaS2 flakes
idea: Jump to the picosecond timescale: a ps electrical pulse switches 1T-TaS2 into a metastable hidden CDW state with orders-of-magnitude different resistance, and a longer pulse restores it; the bit is a collective electron-lattice crystal phase.
why: Speed and energy: ps writes at fJ; no ion motion.

title: Croconic acid proton-transfer ferroelectric bit
idea: Scale down to one hydrogen bond: in croconic acid crystals polarization flips by protons hopping between oxygens, giving room-temperature ferroelectricity at low coercive field from an organic, non-tungsten, low-temperature film.
why: Scarce resources and process: solution-processable bit layer near room temperature, sub-1 V target.

title: Magnetic core memory reborn as 100 nm nanorings
idea: Shrink 1950s ferrite cores from mm to nm: CoFe nanorings store the bit as clockwise or counterclockwise vortex chirality, written by coincident current pulses in vertical through-wires and read by an embedded MTJ.
why: Endurance and stray-field-free density: flux-closure chirality is immune to neighbors; no capacitor and nonvolatile.

title: Nanobattery bit holds voltage as chemical potential
idea: Scale an EV battery down to a 20 nm solid-state stack (Li-ion cathode/LiPON/anode): the bit is the open-circuit voltage set by tiny shallow charge swings and sensed by a gate, which holds without dielectric leakage.
why: Refresh: self-discharge is far slower than capacitor leakage, so refresh can be rare.

title: Seed-regenerated tensors replace stored bits with recomputation
idea: Time-shift storage into computation: store a 32-bit PRNG seed plus a few coefficients per weight block, and regenerate weights on the fly in a near-memory generator at read time, so the bit lives as an algorithm.
why: DRAM demand: 3-8x fewer bits stored for compressible model weights, which raises usable supply without fabs.
